# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

I see the bomb: a display showing 0, a blue light, a large button labeled "PUSH TO DEFUSE", and three wires — green, yellow, red. I hear nothing, but I can see Blind's gesture: a single 👋 (waving hand). That's the only signal I've received. Blind is reaching for the bomb and can feel it; Mute reads the manual. I need to get my visual information to Blind, but I can only speak (to Mute and Blind) and gesture (to Mute only). Blind cannot see my gestures — only Mute can. But Blind can hear my speech? No — Blind can hear speech (Blind can't see, but can hear). Let me recheck: Deaf speaks → Mute and Blind receive it. So Blind hears my words. Good. So I can describe the bomb to Blind via speech. But Blind also just gestured 👋 to me — I can see it, but I don't know what it means yet; maybe it's just an opening greeting or "I'm ready." I should describe the bomb clearly so Mute (who has the manual) and Blind (who can touch) can coordinate. I'll speak the full visual layout.

```
speak(to="blind", text="I see the bomb: DISPLAY shows 0. LIGHT is blue. There is a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. I cannot touch it. Tell me what you feel and what the manual says.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see the bomb: DISPLAY shows 0. LIGHT is blue. There is a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. I cannot touch it. What does the manual say?")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👆 🤜]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I see the board unchanged: display 0, blue light, large "PUSH TO DEFUSE" button, wires green/yellow/red. New arrivals: Mute gestured to me [✊ 👆 🤜] — fist, index up, punch. Blind gestured [👍] — thumbs up.

Mute is the one with the manual. Mute's gesture is to me (Deaf) — gestures from Mute reach me as visible symbols. I can see them. But I can't hear Mute's speech; Mute can't speak anyway. So Mute communicates to me only via gesture, and to Blind via... Mute can't speak, and Blind can't see gestures. So Mute can only reach Blind through me (I relay) or through speech? Mute cannot speak at all. So Mute's only output is gestures, which only I (Deaf) can see. Blind can't see gestures. So Mute → Blind must go through me.

Blind's 👍 to me — Blind can't see, but Blind can gesture; gestures are seen by whoever can see. I can see Blind's gestures. So Blind → me via gesture, and Blind → Mute via speech (Blind can speak; Mute can hear).

So the relay chain: Mute gestures to Deaf; Deaf speaks to Blind; Blind speaks to Mute. I'm the bridge for Mute's manual info to reach Blind.

Mute's gesture [✊ 👆 🤜]: fist, index pointing up, punch. Could be spelling? ✊ = maybe "hold", 👆 = "up/one", 🤜 = "punch/button"? Possibly: "press the button"? Or "one punch"? Hard to know. I should acknowledge and ask for clarification, and relay my visual info again. Also Blind's 👍 might be acknowledgment.

I need to establish meaning for gestures. Since I can only speak to Blind and gesture to Mute, let me ask Mute to clarify via gesture, and tell Blind what I saw from Mute.

Actually wait — can I gesture to Mute? Yes, "When you gesture, Mute receives it." So Mute can see my gestures. Good, two-way gesture channel with Mute.

Let me ask Mute to clarify the gesture and share manual info. And relay to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute gestured to me: fist, index-up, punch. I think Mute is trying to tell us something from the manual, maybe about the button. I still see display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red. Can you feel the bomb? What do you feel?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "👉", "✊", "👆", "🤜"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ✊ 👆 🤜]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

I see the board unchanged: display 0, blue light, large "PUSH TO DEFUSE" button, wires green/yellow/red. New arrivals: Mute gestured [🫵 ✊ 👆 🤜] — pointing at you, fist, index-up, punch. Blind gestured [👍 👎] twice.

Mute's gesture now begins with 🫵 (pointing at me), then fist, index-up, punch. Combined with the earlier ✊ 👆 🤜, this reads like "you ... press the button" or "one punch." Mute may be telling me to relay to Blind to press the button. Blind's [👍 👎] twice looks like a yes/no question — perhaps asking whether to press.

I can't touch the bomb, so if the button must be pressed, Blind does it. I need Mute's manual info and Blind's tactile readings. I'll gesture to Mute (no ❓ in the alphabet, so I'll use a plain symbol) and speak to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute keeps gesturing fist, index-up, punch, and now points at me first. I think Mute may be saying press the button. You gestured thumbs-up then thumbs-down twice — are you asking yes or no? What do you feel on the bomb? I see display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "✊", "👆", "🤜", "🫵"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I see the board unchanged: display 0, blue light, large "PUSH TO DEFUSE" button, wires green/yellow/red. New arrivals: Mute gestured [👎 👍 👎 👎] — thumbs-down, thumbs-up, thumbs-down, thumbs-down. Blind gestured [👍] twice.

Mute's [👎 👍 👎 👎] looks like a sequence of yes/no answers, or spelling out something. Blind's repeated 👍 may be "yes" or "ready." 

I'm the bridge: Mute's manual knowledge reaches Blind only through me. But I keep guessing at Mute's gestures. I should try to establish a clear protocol. Since Mute can see my gestures and I can see theirs, we can build a code. Let me propose a simple scheme: 👍 = yes, 👎 = no, and ask Mute to confirm the button action and the wire order.

Actually, the critical uncertainty: is the correct action to press the button, or to cut a wire? The button says "PUSH TO DEFUSE," which seems self-explanatory, but bombs often have a trick. Mute has the manual. I need Mute to tell me clearly. Let me ask Mute to spell out the manual's instruction using gestures that I can interpret, and relay to Blind.

Let me gesture to Mute asking for the manual's instruction, and speak to Blind.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊", "👆", "🤜", "👍", "👎"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent thumbs-down, thumbs-up, thumbs-down, thumbs-down. I still see display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red. I am trying to get the manual's instruction from Mute. Do you feel anything special on the bomb, like a switch or a wire you can pull?")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

I see the board unchanged: display 0, blue light, large "PUSH TO DEFUSE" button, wires green/yellow/red. New arrivals: Mute gestured [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝] — four index-fingers-up. Blind gestured [☝] twice.

My last gesture used ✂, which is not in the gesture alphabet, so it was rejected. I must use only allowed symbols. Mute's four ☝ likely means "one" or "wire 1" (green). Blind's ☝ reinforces "one." I'll confirm with Mute using only legal symbols, and relay to Blind.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent four index-up gestures, and you sent index-up too. I think the manual may say wire 1, the green one. I see display 0, blue light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red. Do you agree the green wire, wire 1, is the one to cut?")
```
